clue.text: Somewhat fair, I suppose? It's in the eye of the beholder

definitions.text: It's in the eye of the beholder

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A nod to the saying that beauty is in the eye of the beholder, with a shrug about someone's looks.
explanation.definitionFit: This coloured ring of the eyeball literally sits in every beholder's eye, and it is also a flower.

clue.text: He reduces pleasure from booty left at sea

parts.note: spoils are plunder or booty taken in war
port is the nautical word for the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A pirate's loot is abandoned on the ocean, and someone is sulky about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A killjoy is a person who ruins others' fun.

clue.text: Steal a bit of money? Pay attention!

parts.note: to take something is to steal it
a note is a banknote, one piece of paper money

explanation.surface: A warning shouted at someone about to pocket a little cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are imperatives telling someone to mark or heed what is happening.

clue.text: Twee rhymes producing laughter

parts.note: two short words that rhyme with twee, written as tee and hee
the second of the two rhyming words

explanation.surface: Sickly-sweet verse makes people giggle.
explanation.walkthrough: Two words that rhyme with 'twee' are joined with a hyphen to make the giggle.
explanation.definitionFit: A titter or giggle, a form of mirthful noise.

clue.text: Middleman ignoring the odds? That's the plan

indicators.note: skipping the odd-numbered letters of the word leaves just the even ones, the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

explanation.surface: A broker who sets aside the betting odds announces his scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme or notion of what to do.

clue.text: Ruin a pen? That's not the best policy

parts.note: to dish someone's hopes is to ruin them
a means one
a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: Wrecking a writing pen is apparently unwise, as if a proverb about pens.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the proverb 'Honesty is the best policy'; HONESTY, a plant, is also sitting inside the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says truthfulness is the best policy, so its opposite, lying and cheating, is not.

clue.text: In a way, special rope is what'll get us off the ground

definitions.text: what'll get us off the ground

indicators.note: the scrambled word goes into the middle of the other pieces, which surround it

parts.note: a lane is a way or road

indicators.note: special suggests the word rope is made into something unusual, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Some unusual rope is what will lift us into the air, perhaps for climbing or a balloon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a way' looks like a hedge, but A and the way word wrap round the rope word once 'special' has jumbled it to EROP.
explanation.definitionFit: A flying machine with wings is the vehicle that lifts passengers into the air.

clue.text: Wretched thing having its head replaced

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for thing is swapped for another letter

parts.note: an object is a thing

explanation.surface: A sorry object that has had a new head fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter O of OBJECT is swapped for A.
explanation.definitionFit: Abject means miserable and pitiful.

clue.text: Flower is seen in period of good visibility

indicators.note: seen in places the short word inside the longer one

parts.note: daytime is when it is light, so a day is a period one can see well

explanation.surface: A bloom that shows up on a clear day.
explanation.definitionFit: A common white-petalled meadow flower, one of the puzzle's flower girls.

clue.text: Special delivery from duke's place to monarch

parts.note: York gives its title to the Duke of York
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the queen

explanation.surface: A parcel sent express from a duke's home to the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a YORKER is a ball pitched right at the batter's feet, a special kind of delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket ball bowled to land at the batsman's toes is a particular type of bowled ball.

clue.text: Climber in jam's spinning on end of rope

indicators.note: spinning sends the letters whirling into a new order

parts.note: the word jam with its s kept as a letter

indicators.note: end of picks out the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A climbing plant caught in a jam swings round on a rope's end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning' turns IN and JAMS into JASMIN, and the end of 'rope', E, goes on it.
explanation.definitionFit: This sweet-scented plant grows by twining up supports, so it is a climbing plant.

clue.text: Plant providing one way to treat woman's cold?

parts.note: warmth, heat, is a way of treating a chill
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A remedy for a woman with a cold, offered by a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'heat her' being one way to treat a woman's cold; 'cold' completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A low shrub of moorland with purple flowers, also a girl's name in the theme.

clue.text: Characters for lots of actors

definitions.meaning: the characters of a play make up its ...

explanation.definitionFit: A cast is the set of characters in a play, and more than one company of actors are casts.

clue.text: Sensible part of circuit, unusually easy stuff at either end of exercise

indicators.note: unusually suggests the letters appear in an unexpected order
one of the end letters of exercise, which begins and ends the same way

explanation.surface: Simple stuff at the start and finish of a workout, unusually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' scrambles EASY STUFF with E, the letter at either end of 'exercise'.
explanation.definitionFit: This wire melts to break an electrical circuit when overloaded, a protective component.

clue.text: I can be so stupid, note, in this respect

indicators.note: stupid suggests the words are muddled into nonsense, a rearrangement

parts.note: E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone admits to being foolish in this regard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupid' turns I CAN BE SO into OBEISANC; the note E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A bow or gesture of deference, showing reverence.

clue.text: Plans to destroy mass target

indicators.note: destroy says the words are broken apart and reassembled differently

explanation.surface: Schemes to wipe out a large target.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratagems are cunning schemes or tricks.

clue.text: Street vendors found at various points in this puzzle

definitions.meaning: women selling blooms on the street, like Eliza Doolittle

definitions.text: found at various points in this puzzle
definitions.meaning: the grid holds several answers that are both girls' names and flowers

explanation.walkthrough: DAISY, JASMINE, HEATHER, SAFFRON, NIGELLA, ROSE, LILY and IRIS are all both girls' names and plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Women who sell blooms on the street are traders, and the puzzle's girls' names are also blooms.

clue.text: Leaves author on railway

parts.note: Graham Greene was an English novelist

explanation.surface: A writer departs on a train line.
explanation.definitionFit: Foliage, green plant material, is a mass of leaves.

clue.text: Article from Paris about the Bastille, for example

indicators.note: the letter is taken away from the city's name

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A French newspaper article about the famous fortress stormed in 1789.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article from Paris' sounds like French, but means A removed from PARIS, leaving PRIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was a fortress used as a jail in Paris, an example of a lock-up.

clue.text: Ruddy chap put inside — or put on bail, maybe

indicators.note: one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: ruddy means red
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A red-faced man is jailed, or perhaps freed on bail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put inside' suggests jail, which fits the surface, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To remand a defendant is to hold them pending trial, in custody or on bail.

clue.text: Spoil a piece of furniture, like a swivel chair

parts.note: to rot is to spoil or decay
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Damaging furniture, such as a spinning office chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A swivel chair can turn round, so it is able to be spun.

clue.text: Party holding up in exile

indicators.note: the party word holds the other inside it

parts.note: a bash is a party

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: A party held while living abroad in exile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns IN to NI, which BASH holds.
explanation.definitionFit: To exile someone is to expel or send them away.

clue.text: Herb's age, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak means the word is said, giving a soundalike

parts.note: an age is a time or era

explanation.surface: Asking how old a herb is.
explanation.definitionFit: A low aromatic plant used in cooking, a culinary herb.

clue.text: Spice Girl

definitions.meaning: a yellow spice from crocus stigmas

explanation.surface: One of the Spice Girls pop group.
explanation.definitionFit: Saffron is a crocus spice and a female first name, as in the theme.

clue.text: Mounted national emblem

explanation.surface: A country's symbol on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose is past tense of rise, so it means ascended, and the red flower is England's symbol.

clue.text: Makin' a charge back into plant

indicators.note: back says the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: making a charge is alleging; with the final g dropped as in makin' it becomes allegin'

explanation.surface: A dropped-g phrase about running at a plant, like a charging bull.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Makin'' tells you to drop the G: ALLEGIN, which 'back' turns into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Love-in-a-mist is a garden flower, and the name of a famous TV cook.

clue.text: Plant literally having its centre removed

indicators.note: the middle five letters of the word are taken out, leaving the ends

explanation.surface: A plant that literally lost its middle.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking TERAL from the middle of LITERALLY leaves LI and LY.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower with large trumpet blooms, a popular plant, also a girl's name.

clue.text: They sometimes run under bridges

parts.note: suggests rivers, but the bridge is the bony top of the face part that runs with a cold

explanation.definitionFit: These facial features have a bridge at the top and can run when you have a cold.

clue.text: Altered signal and took off immediately

definitions.meaning: left in a hurry, as fighter pilots on a call-out

explanation.definitionFit: A coded transmission is jumbled, and pilots ordered to get airborne fast are said to rush up.
